candidates.name: Abdul El-Sayed
candidates.bio: Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate, former Michigan health director and public health advocate.

quotes.text: A.I. should be governed by public-interest standards, not just market incentives. We need federal AI safety rules that protect workers and communities.
Michigan workers built this state. We need to ensure AI systems don't eliminate jobs without a transition plan for working families.
Generative AI companies should be required to disclose training data sources and ensure fair compensation for creators whose work was used.

aiPolicy.stance: Strong federal AI safety and regulation
keyPositions: Federal AI licensing framework for high-risk systems
Mandatory impact assessments for AI deployment in critical sectors
Worker protection and transition funds for AI-displaced workers
Transparency requirements for training data and algorithms

partyAlignment.description: Strongly aligned with Democratic Party AI safety platform
deviations: Slightly more labor-focused than national party platform

policyProjection.ifElected: If elected, El-Sayed would likely push for comprehensive federal AI regulation including a national AI licensing board, strong worker protections in the AI sector, and mandatory algorithmic transparency. His administration would likely prioritize labor protections over innovation speed.
keyInitiatives: National AI Safety and Standards Board
AI Copyright and Creator Protection Act

candidates.name: Mike Rogers
candidates.bio: Republican candidate for U.S. Senate, former U.S. Representative and cybersecurity expert.

quotes.text: America must lead in AI innovation. Over-regulation will hand the competitive advantage to China and Russia. We need light-touch rules that protect security without strangling innovation.
The best regulation is no regulation. Let the private sector innovate, and we'll step in only when national security is at stake.
Cybersecurity and national defense must be priorities in AI policy. We need to secure our AI systems against foreign threats while maintaining our technological edge.

keyPositions: Sector-specific, self-regulatory approaches to AI governance

partyAlignment.description: Aligned with Republican emphasis on innovation and lighter regulation
deviations: Slightly more focused on national security than mainstream GOP platform

policyProjection.ifElected: If elected, Rogers would likely block comprehensive federal AI regulation in favor of sector-specific oversight. His focus would be on national security and maintaining U.S. competitiveness in AI. He would resist labor-focused regulations and advocate for minimal compliance burdens on industry.
keyInitiatives: AI Cybersecurity and National Security Framework
